title: Performance Comparison of Conventional Synchronous Reluctance Machines and PM-Assisted Types with Combined Star-Delta Winding

source.citation: M. N. F. Ibrahim, E. Rashad, P. Sergeant, Energies 10(10):1500, 2017

related.citation: M. N. Ibrahim, P. Sergeant, E. M. Rashad, Energies 9(11):942, 2016
related.use: The same lamination's stator dimensions (Fig. A1: 5.15 mm teeth, 6.80 mm tips) and slot area (100 mm2), cross-checks of Fig. 3a.

machine.topology: inner rotor with three flux barriers per pole (ferrite-assisted in two prototypes); 36 slots with a single-layer distributed star or combined star-delta winding
machine.symmetry: Full cross-section; a sliding band in the gap turns the rotor. dq currents from the winding's phase-A axis and the rotor's d-axis at zero.

stator_steel.reason: M270-50A (Table 1) is not in FEMM's library; M-19 is its usual AISI counterpart (B at 2500/5000/10000 A/m: 1.593/1.664/1.763 T, against about 1.55/1.65/1.76 T typical of M270-50A).

rotor_steel.reason: M330-50A (Table 1) is not in FEMM's library; M-36 is its usual AISI counterpart (1.528/1.614/1.730 T at 2500/5000/10000 A/m, about 0.02 T below typical M330-50A).

stacking_factor.reason: Not stated; 0.97 is typical of 0.5 mm laminations (the library entries carry 0.955 for 0.36 mm). The literal reading, no stacking factor (a solid steel in the 2D FE), is the control.

shaft_material.reason: Not stated; Fig. 7 shows no flux in the shaft (below 0.13 T), as for a non-magnetic shaft. Ibrahim 2016's shaft-steel control on this lamination moved its torque by 0.0%.

gaps.note: The paper gives no barrier dimensions (they are optimized in its refs. [17, 18], conference papers not cached), but Fig. 3a is vector art drawn to scale (its four circles check within 0.05 mm) and its barriers coincide with the authors' Maxwell plot (Fig. 7a). They are not Ibrahim 2016's Table A1 prototype: widths 8.0, 6.0 and 3.66 mm (not 6, 4, 3), middle sections 30, 25 and 15 mm long (not 25, 19, 12), ends at 8.2, 16.4 and 29.8 degrees from the d-axis, ribs 0.84, 0.74 and 0.55 mm. Legs run from the middle sections' corners, so flux_barrier_rotor (legs as wide as the middle) cannot draw them; the outlines are built as data (entity_pattern).

gaps.affects: slot leakage and tooth saturation, slightly
gaps.note: Fig. 3a gives the slot: 5.14 mm parallel teeth, a 2.80 mm opening with 0.42 mm walls, a curved shoe underside from the walls to the tooth sides at 57.52 mm, a flat bottom at 72.51 mm; drawn area 101.1 mm2, Ibrahim 2016's stated 100 mm2. The curved underside is built as a straight taper and the flat bottom as an arc.

M-19 for M270-50A and M-36 for M330-50A; control steel-neighbours (M-15 and M-27). Bracketed before freezing: the neighbours' B is 0.01 T lower (stator) and 0.03-0.05 T higher (rotor) at 2500-10000 A/m; with the d-axis iron carrying about half the d-axis MMF at rated current, about +1% torque (ibrahim-2016-synrm's steel-m45 control moved its torque -0.9%).

0.97, typical of 0.5 mm grades; control solid-steel (1.0, no stacking factor in the FE). Bracketed before freezing: 3% more iron flux at a given field where the iron saturates, about +1 to +2% torque at rated current, less at half current.
Figs. 8, 9, 14, 16 and 24 label the current axis I_RMS, and the rated current is their curves' end: 12.23 A is rms.

gaps.affects: torque ripple (Figs. 11-13); not the average torque
gaps.note: Maxwell computed the delta currents in a coupled circuit; their fundamental is (i_a - i_b)/3 (Fig. 13: about 10 A peak against the star coils' 17.3 A), imposed here. The zero-sequence third harmonic (about 11% of the fundamental) produces no fundamental MMF; it adds ripple, which is not a target.

Fig. 4 (registered to Fig. 3a by 24 corners, 0.18 pt rms) fills each barrier's middle section: its yellow fills are 0.42-0.53 mm thinner and 0.3-1.0 mm shorter than the sections, about the outline's stroke width, so the magnets are built as the whole sections (uncertainty 0.5 mm). The direction is the q-axis, against the armature's q-axis flux (a PM-assisted rotor; Fig. 5's PM curves are positive at alpha = 0); checked from the construction's dq frame: +q is outward at the 45-degree q-axis, so the magnets there point inward (magdir [225, 135, 45, 315]). Linear magnet through Br 0.39 T and Hc 234 kA/m (mu_r 1.326).

gaps.affects: every torque at the optimal angle
gaps.note: Not tabulated: Fig. 5 puts it near 55 (S, Sd) and 52 degrees (PM rotors) at full current and 46/42 degrees at half. Each sweep spans it with 5-degree steps and takes the parabolic vertex (a 0.1% bound for a curve like Fig. 5's).

variants.purpose: The combined star-delta winding (Fig. 3b: -a, +ca, +ca, +c, -bc, -bc, -b, +ab, +ab from 0 to 80 degrees): star coils of 26 turns carrying the line currents, delta coils of 45 turns carrying (i_a - i_b)/3 and so on; the plain rotor.
The star winding with Y30BH ferrite magnets filling each barrier's middle section (Fig. 4), magnetized to oppose the q-axis armature flux.
The combined star-delta winding with the ferrite-assisted rotor.

coverage.reproduced: The 2D FEM torque at the optimal current angle of all four prototypes: at the data tips of Fig. 24 (acceptance, 1%) and at full and half rated current (Fig. 5, digitized), and the PM rotors' torque with the current on the d-axis (Fig. 5).
coverage.not_reproduced: Torque ripple (Figs. 6, 11, 14; mesh-noise dominated, and the delta coils' circulating currents are left out), power factor (Figs. 15, 16, 23: the paper's includes effects a 2D magnetostatic model lacks), losses and efficiency (Figs. 18-30), the delta currents' harmonics (Figs. 12-13), the saliency ratios (Fig. 10) and the measured torques (Figs. 22, 24), which the findings compare without acceptance.
coverage.pre_solve_estimate: From ibrahim-2016-synrm's recorded FEMM build of this lamination (20.66 N m at 165 A per slot, rms; torque going as the 1.55 power of the slot current between its rms and amplitude readings): 159 A per slot (26 turns at 12.23/2 A) gives about 19.5 N m against Fig. 5's 17.50 (+11%), 137.7 A per slot (10.59 A) about 15.6 against 13.89 (+12%); that build's inductances (Ld 17.4, Lq 1.9 mH at 15 turns) scaled by the turns squared give 14.7 N m at 10.59 A (+6%). Its rotor is narrower (Table A1), so these bound the outcome loosely: a 27-36% excess, as in 2016, would point at the shared construction (stator, winding, steel, depth); agreement at the 2016 paper. About 150k elements (ibrahim-2016-synrm meshed 140k with the same sizes): 170 solves per level, 8 levels, about 9 s per solve.
